newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-STEELERS SIGN KICKER CHRIS JACKE AWAY FROM PACKERS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-STEELERS SIGN KICKER CHRIS JACKE AWAY FROM PACKERS.

text.p: The Pittsburgh Steelers Tuesday signed unrestricted free agent place kicker Chris Jacke away from the Green Bay Packers and released veteran kicker Norm Johnson.
The 31-year-old Jacke played the first eight seasons of his career with the Packers and helped them to a Super Bowl victory last season.
He had 114 points in the regular season, including a league-best 51 extra points, and a 21-for-27 performance on field goals.

Jacke holds 13 Green Bay team records and shares four others. He is 173-of-224 on field goals with 301 extra points in his career, leaving him three points shy of the late Don Hutson's all-time Packers scoring record of 823 points.
Jacke's success rate of 65.4 percent on field goals of 50-or-more yards is the second-best in league history and his overall field-goal percentage of .772 is 11th-best all-time.

The 37-year-old Johnson is eighth on the NFL all-time scoring list with 1,452 points, sixth with 552 extra points and ninth with 300 field goals. In 1995, he set Pittsburgh team records with 141 points and 34 field goals.
Last season Johnson connected on 23-of-30 field-goal attempts and 37 extra points.
